title: Reading the Benefit a Policy Has Consumed in Its Term
content:
How much benefit a policy of the Travel Protection Plans has consumed in its term is read from the policy's
own claim record where that record is able to answer, and from the policy record itself where it is not.

## The three readings

1. Where the policy's claim record carries a recovery received from a liable third party, the benefit consumed
   is worked out from the claim record as the payments made less the recoveries received against them.
2. Where the claim record carries no such recovery and more than one payment stands on it, the benefit consumed
   is the sum of the payments standing on the claim record.
3. In every other case the benefit consumed is the figure the policy record shows consumed.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A claim record carrying payments of 600.00 and 450.00 and a recovery of 200.00 received against one of them
falls under the first reading, and the benefit consumed is 850.00. The same record without the recovery falls
under the second, more than one payment standing on it, and the benefit consumed is 1050.00. A record carrying
one payment alone and no recovery falls under the third, and the benefit consumed is whatever figure the policy
record shows consumed, which need not equal that single payment. A record carrying no payment at all falls under
the third likewise.
